# Worked examples: rulebooks the hobby praises and criticises

Cite these by name when justifying a recommendation — a designer trusts 'Fantasy Flight splits Learn to Play from Rules Reference' more than an abstract principle.

## Praised

| Game / publisher | Aspect | What specifically | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fantasy Flight Games (Marvel Champions, Arkham Horror LCG, Descent 3E) | Dual-document model | Condensed 'Learn to Play' to get started + an extensive alphabetical 'Rules Reference' with a detailed index; users report finding anything 'in seconds'. | [BGG: Best Rule Book (In Your Humble Opinion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1932289/best-rule-book-in-your-humble-opinion) |
| Root (Leder Games) | Walkthrough / Learning-to-Play book | Ships a scripted walkthrough book alongside a formal rules reference; the reference explicitly tells you which book to read based on your learning style. | [Playing By The Rules (incl. Paul Grogan interview) – Punchboard](https://www.punchboard.co.uk/playing-by-the-rules/) |
| Arcs (Leder Games) | Tone + component descriptions + repacking diagram | Warm, honest, casual voice ('expect a long, tedious first game'); each component gets a short contextual description; even a labelled repacking guide. | [The Stonemaier Games Style Guide](https://stonemaiergames.com/the-stonemaier-games-style-guide/) |
| Alea series (Puerto Rico, San Juan, Castles of Burgundy) | Marginal summaries | Full explanation in the main column, one-line summary in the margin — teaching and reference on the same spread. 'The Alea series all have the same style and it has made learning them a breeze.' | [BGG: Good Rulebooks (2021)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2644979/good-rulebooks) |
| Puerto Rico | Edge-case handling | Every building carries its clarifications directly beneath its description, largely eliminating the need for an online FAQ. | [Laying Down the Law (a guide to rulebook writing) – I Slay the Dragon](https://islaythedragon.com/featured/laying-down-the-law-a-guide-to-rulebook-writing/) |
| Dominion | Keyword discipline + card appendix | Only a handful of keywords (Action, Buy, Gain, Card), used with total consistency; a per-card appendix covers odd combos, including cross-expansion ones. | [Laying Down the Law (a guide to rulebook writing) – I Slay the Dragon](https://islaythedragon.com/featured/laying-down-the-law-a-guide-to-rulebook-writing/) |
| Uwe Rosenberg rulebooks (A Feast for Odin, Agricola later editions, Terra Mystica) | Order of presentation + 'Uwe Says' tips | Strong sense of the right order to introduce ideas, examples attached to most concepts, digestible chunks, and sprinkled tip boxes. | [BGG: Best Written Rulebooks as of 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2323149/best-written-rulebooks-as-of-2019) |
| Vital Lacerda games (Lisboa, On Mars) — ed. Paul Grogan | Density of worked examples | Examples 'help the rules congeal' when learning or clarifying; a professional rules editor works on the books from the start. | [BGG: What makes a good rulebook? (2021)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2784900/what-makes-a-good-rulebook) |
| Gloomhaven | Graphical index | Picture-led index repeatedly named best-in-class for mid-game look-up in a dungeon crawler. | [BGG: Glossary or alphabetical TOC/Index really needed?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2641261/glossary-or-alphabetical-tocindex-really-needed) |
| Gloomhaven: Jaws of the Lion | Tutorial rulebook | Progressive-disclosure teaching across the first scenarios; named by Stonemaier as a rulebook to study for its tutorial. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Combat Commander: Europe / Fighting Formations (Chad Jensen) | Wargame reference craft | 'No filler, everything laid out logically, in easy to understand terms, with examples' — TOC, glossary and index all present. | [BGG: Good Rulebooks (2021)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2644979/good-rulebooks) |
| Here I Stand / GCACW (Ed Beach) | Complex-game rules writing | Repeatedly named as the best rulebook author for genuinely complex games. | [Best rulebooks? – There Will Be Games forum](https://therewillbe.games/forum/10-ameritrash/124383-best-rulebooks) |
| Twilight Struggle Deluxe | Numbered-section navigation | Old Avalon Hill numbering makes look-up fast; 'flows really well and makes looking things up a snap'. | [Best rulebooks? – There Will Be Games forum](https://therewillbe.games/forum/10-ameritrash/124383-best-rulebooks) |
| Splendor | Brevity | A four-page rulebook for a strategy game — proof that sparse can be complete. | [Laying Down the Law (a guide to rulebook writing) – I Slay the Dragon](https://islaythedragon.com/featured/laying-down-the-law-a-guide-to-rulebook-writing/) |
| Belfort | Explaining many moving parts | 'The game seems simpler than it is, largely because of the excellent rulebook.' | [Laying Down the Law (a guide to rulebook writing) – I Slay the Dragon](https://islaythedragon.com/featured/laying-down-the-law-a-guide-to-rulebook-writing/) |
| Roll Player | Fine-grained section breakdown | 16 pages, generously spaced, split into more (not fewer) categories, back cover as quick reference; 'you felt like you already had a game under your belt after you read it'. | [BGG: Best Rule Book (In Your Humble Opinion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1932289/best-rule-book-in-your-humble-opinion) |
| Attika | Layout + forgotten-rules list | Clear headers, disciplined bold, two-column split to mirror a two-option choice, and a closing list of rules often forgotten in a first game. | [BGG: Best Rule Book (In Your Humble Opinion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1932289/best-rule-book-in-your-humble-opinion) |
| Russian Railroads | All-round craft | 'Logical, straightforward layout; clear pictures and examples; well written; pleasing to the eyes.' | [BGG: Best Rule Book (In Your Humble Opinion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1932289/best-rule-book-in-your-humble-opinion) |
| The Gallerist | Clarity + organisation | 'Extremely clear explanations, well-organized, nicely illustrated.' | [BGG: Best Rule Book (In Your Humble Opinion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1932289/best-rule-book-in-your-humble-opinion) |
| Galactic Cruise | Organisation | Named by Stonemaier as the rulebook to study for organisation. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Dungeon Lords (CGE) | Humour that aids retention | Divisive but named by Stonemaier as the book to study for humour; a BGG user notes its lore actively helps rules stick. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Barcelona | Historical context | Named by Stonemaier as the rulebook to study for the use of history/context. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Origin Story | Serving different player types | Named by Stonemaier for accommodating varied player counts and experience levels within one book. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Dawn of the Zeds | Multiple-rulebook architecture | Named by Stonemaier as the study case for splitting content across several books. | [What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games](https://stonemaiergames.com/what-makes-a-great-rulebook/) |
| Mechanica / Surrealist Dinner Party (Resonym) | Attention engineering | Deliberately faded or upside-down text to stop new players reading advanced sections too early. Tom Vasel: 'One of the better written rulebooks I've ever seen.' | [Resonym | Writing Rulebooks](https://resonym.com/writing-rulebooks/) |
| Through the Ages: A New Story of Civilization | Complex-game clarity | Named on BGG as an excellent example of a rulebook for a heavy game. | [BGG: Best Written Rulebooks as of 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2323149/best-written-rulebooks-as-of-2019) |
| SpaceCorp | Modern reference layout | Offered as a starting point for designers looking at contemporary best practice. | [BGG: Best Written Rulebooks as of 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2323149/best-written-rulebooks-as-of-2019) |
| Splotter titles | Breaking complexity down + player aids | 'All fairly complex games but the rules break the complexity down into something much more manageable'; player aids so good the book is rarely needed. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Raptor | Anticipating questions | 'Seems to make a point to hit every possible question you could have about the game, but in a way that is wonderfully organized.' | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Merchants & Marauders | Rulebook + player aid partnership | Heavy information load absorbed on first read; the player aid carries the exceptions that normally trip players up. | [Best rulebooks? – There Will Be Games forum](https://therewillbe.games/forum/10-ameritrash/124383-best-rulebooks) |
| BattleLore / Days of Wonder format | Progressive scenarios | Each intro scenario introduces new concepts, so depth arrives gradually without treating the reader as a beginner forever. | [BGG: Examples of well-written game rules?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/286303/examples-of-well-written-game-rules) |
| Ark Nova | Card-specific appendix | Alphabetical per-card clarification appendix named as the good pattern for resolving edge cases. | [BGG: Rulebooks and text comprehension. A history of misunderstandings.](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3538423/rulebooks-and-text-comprehension-a-history-of-misu) |
| Brass: Birmingham | 'Oft-missed rules' section | A short closing section listing commonly misunderstood rules. | [BGG: Rulebooks and text comprehension. A history of misunderstandings.](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3538423/rulebooks-and-text-comprehension-a-history-of-misu) |
| Dune: Imperium | Single-page symbol reference | One page that collects every symbol used in the game. | [BGG: Rulebooks and text comprehension. A history of misunderstandings.](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3538423/rulebooks-and-text-comprehension-a-history-of-misu) |
| Obsession (Kayenta Games) | Rulebook + separate glossary | 25,000+ words of reference material split into a rulebook and a standalone glossary; designer publicly maintains an itemised errata thread. | [BGG: OFFICIAL Obsession Rulebook and Glossary (errata thread)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2003488/official-obsession-rulebook-and-glossary-downloads) |

## Criticised

| Game | Failure mode | What specifically | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island (1st ed.) | Errors + vagueness + layout | The most-cited bad rulebook in the hobby. Designer Ignacy Trzewiczek has acknowledged serious errors; vague descriptions leave when/how actions can be taken unclear; inconsistent graphic design compounds it. Spawned a large fan FAQ/errata ecosystem. | [4 terrible board game rulebooks that really don’t rule – Going Analog](https://www.goinganalogshow.com/article/230/worst-board-game-rulebooks-manuals) |
| First Martians: Adventures on the Red Planet | Repeat of the same failures | Named by professional editor Paul Grogan as a game a poor rulebook killed; its BGG rules/errata thread ran to hundreds of posts. | [Playing By The Rules (incl. Paul Grogan interview) – Punchboard](https://www.punchboard.co.uk/playing-by-the-rules/) |
| Batman: Gotham City Chronicles | Structure + errata volume | Named by Paul Grogan; seven pages of errata/FAQ on BGG, plus threads pleading with the publisher over rules and player aids. | [Playing By The Rules (incl. Paul Grogan interview) – Punchboard](https://www.punchboard.co.uk/playing-by-the-rules/) |
| Mice and Mystics | No index | Widely liked game, repeatedly cited for a rulebook with no index; players report significant time lost looking rules up. | [BGG: Worst rulebook ever!](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1554960/worst-rulebook-ever) |
| Space Base | No usable index | Card-list 'index' with meaningless ship classes, not alphabetical, so every edge case becomes minutes of page-flipping or a BGG search. | [4 terrible board game rulebooks that really don’t rule – Going Analog](https://www.goinganalogshow.com/article/230/worst-board-game-rulebooks-manuals) |
| Kemet: Blood and Sand | Hidden rules + contradictory wording | Critical rules appear inside the components list; instructions confusing or contradictory; boxout examples make simple rules harder. | [4 terrible board game rulebooks that really don’t rule – Going Analog](https://www.goinganalogshow.com/article/230/worst-board-game-rulebooks-manuals) |
| Coffee Traders | Errors + inconsistent terminology | 1.0 rulebook so confounding the publisher rewrote it two years after release; physical replacement cost players an extra USD 7. | [4 terrible board game rulebooks that really don’t rule – Going Analog](https://www.goinganalogshow.com/article/230/worst-board-game-rulebooks-manuals) |
| Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Rise of the Runelords (1st printing) | Unclear rules + unclear card text | Over 1,500 threads in the game's BGG rules forum plus a long official FAQ/errata; game-specific terms used before being explained. | [BGG: Worst rulebook ever!](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1554960/worst-rulebook-ever) |
| Heroes of Normandie | Disjointed structure + poor translation | Good game, 'rulebook will give you PTSD'; players report constant back-and-forth flipping. | [BGG: Worst rulebook ever!](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1554960/worst-rulebook-ever) |
| Space Hulk: Death Angel – The Card Game | Short but incomprehensible | Only a few pages, yet players could not determine setup or what they were supposed to do — proof that brevity is not clarity. | [BGG: Worst rulebook ever!](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1554960/worst-rulebook-ever) |
| Mage Knight | Rules split across three artefacts | Rules live in the rulebook, on reference cards and elsewhere, with no consistency; reference cards carry rules found nowhere else. | [BGG: Rules missing from Rulebook v1.0 (Triplock)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1803616/rules-missing-from-rulebook-v10) |
| Galaxy Trucker / CGE house style | Humour interleaved with rules | Enjoyable to read once; painful as a reference. Also criticised for teaching via an introductory game whose parts are reused later. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Root | Law-style cross-references | Loved game; rules reference criticised for sending readers back to numbered paragraphs instead of restating the rule. | [BGG: Tutorial differences between videogames and board games](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2681026/tutorial-differences-between-videogames-and-board) |
| Caper | Undefined core term | The word 'set' is used for scoring throughout without ever being defined; two independent groups reached the same wrong reading and played that way for months. | [BGG: Clarity in the Rulebook (Caper)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2395671/clarity-in-the-rulebook) |
| Gloomhaven: Jaws of the Lion | Rules only in the Learn-to-Play book | Glossary omits rules that appear in the tutorial book (e.g. the 10-Curse deck limit), undermining trust in the reference. | [BGG: Sometimes finding the rulebook organization annoying (Jaws of the Lion)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2455924/sometimes-finding-the-rulebook-organization-annoyi) |
| Imperium: Classics / Legends | Omitted solo-bot rule | A commonly-drawn card type the bot should discard was left out entirely, silently making the solo game much harder than intended. | [Playing By The Rules (incl. Paul Grogan interview) – Punchboard](https://www.punchboard.co.uk/playing-by-the-rules/) |
| Agricola (original edition) | Poor first-edition rules | Widely reported as awful in its first edition and substantially improved in later ones — a reminder that reprints are the industry's patch mechanism. | [BGG: Best Written Rulebooks as of 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2323149/best-written-rulebooks-as-of-2019) |
| A Feast for Odin / 7 Wonders | Wrong-booklet problem | Multiple booklets with no obvious rule for which one holds which answer; players report reaching for the wrong one every time. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Ulm | Rules split across two booklets | 'Not actually badly written, but a very unfortunate decision to spread the rules over two separate booklets.' | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Vinhos Deluxe (with KS expansions) | Edition/expansion sprawl | Editions, variants and stretch goals combined haphazardly, with some content only in loose sheets. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Myth (2014) | Kickstarter rulebook failure | USD 900,000+ raised; players reported spending more time deciphering the rulebook than playing. Prompted a 72-page unofficial fan rewrite. | [BGG blog: Every Board Game Rulebook is Awful (Dean Ray Johnson)](https://boardgamegeek.com/blog/13453/every-board-game-rulebook-is-awful) |
| Perdition's Mouth: Abyssal Rift | Merged Overview and Setup + icon/sidebar overload | Documented self-critique by its own rulebook writer; Tom Vasel: 'The rulebook itself, which I thought was very overwrought, it took me a while just to figure out how to play.' | [BGG blog: Every Board Game Rulebook is Awful (Dean Ray Johnson)](https://boardgamegeek.com/blog/13453/every-board-game-rulebook-is-awful) |
| Mysterium | Re-learning friction | Loved game whose rules produce a reliable 'wait, what now?' moment on every refresher read. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Innovation (small-format rules) | Dense keywords in a tiny book | Meld / Tuck / Splay presented so compactly the reader bounces; the game is loved once learned. | [BGG: Worst/Best written rules](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1949478/worstbest-written-rules) |
| Sword & Sorcery: Immortal Souls | No keyword index | Subject-based TOC only; players resort to PDF text search or build their own alphabetical reference over dozens of hours. | [BGG: Glossary or alphabetical TOC/Index really needed?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2641261/glossary-or-alphabetical-tocindex-really-needed) |
| Raising Robots: Pets (expansion) | Icon drift + unstated interactions | Icon in the index did not match the printed cards; rules for repeat activation and timing were never stated. Fixed in the next printing. | [BGG: Pets Rule Book is missing some crucial info](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3271735/pets-rule-book-is-missing-some-crucial-info) |
| Inferno (pre-release rulebook) | Ambiguous requirements + thematic verbs | 'Bring an urchin' vs 'place an urchin'; unclear access requirements; solo setup step contradicted the standard setup. | Triplock | Rules only on reference cards | Trap/countermeasure rules existed only on a reference card that some copies shipped outside the box; the publisher moved them into the book for later printings. | [BGG: Rules missing from Rulebook v1.0 (Triplock)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1803616/rules-missing-from-rulebook-v10) |
| Obsession (1st print run) | Count errors across artefacts | Component counts wrong in the rulebook and glossary; a player aid stated 2 reputation where the board and rules said 4. | [BGG: OFFICIAL Obsession Rulebook and Glossary (errata thread)](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2003488/official-obsession-rulebook-and-glossary-downloads) |
| Race for the Galaxy | Very small body text | Roughly 6-8pt type, legible but repeatedly raised as the reference point for 'too small'. | [BGG: In-depth information about designing a good rulebook](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/897413/in-depth-information-about-designing-a-good-rulebo) |
| Killer Bunnies | Display typography over legibility | Thin font, small size, tight kerning, bold colour outlines — sold after a handful of plays for that reason. | [BGG: Examples of well-written game rules?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/286303/examples-of-well-written-game-rules) |
| Star Fleet Battles | Rules diluted by non-rules text | 'Full of too many words that don't have anything to do with the rules... one liners, strategy ideas and stray thoughts.' | [BGG: Examples of well-written game rules?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/286303/examples-of-well-written-game-rules) |
| Advanced Squad Leader | Legalese density | Single sentences a paragraph long, attempting to cover every eventuality at once; comprehensive but not learnable. | [BGG: Examples of well-written game rules?](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/286303/examples-of-well-written-game-rules) |
